exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 21–26, mark each statement True or False. Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The $$(i,j) \text{-element}$$ in the fundamental matrix $$M$$ is the expected number of visits to the transient state $$j$$ prior to absorption, starting at the transient state $$i$$ .
(T/F) The sum of the column $$j$$ of the fundamental matrix $$M$$ is the expected number of time steps until absorption.
(T/F) The $$(j,i) \text{-element}$$ in the fundamental matrix gives the expected number of visits to state $$i$$ prior to absorption, starting at state $$j$$ .
(T/F) Transit times may be computed directly from the entries in the transition matrix.

(T/F) The probability that the Markov chain starting at state $$i$$ is eventually absorbed by state $$j$$ is the $$(j,i) \text{-element}$$ of the matrix $$A = SM$$ , where $$M$$ is the fundamental matrix of the Markov chain and $$S$$ is that portion of the transition matrix that governs movement from transient states to absorbing states.
(T/F) If $$A$$ is an $$m \times m$$ substochastic matrix, then the entries in $$A^{n}$$ approach $$0$$ as $$n$$ increases.

Since states $$1$$ and $$4$$ are absorbing states, reordering the states as $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 4 \text{,} 2 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ produces the canonical form $$& & \begin{matrix}1 & 4 & 2 & 3\end{matrix} & P & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 & 0 & 1 / 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{matrix}$$ So $$& & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & & & & & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & Q & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}2 \\ 3\end{matrix} & \text{and} & M & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}30 / 19 & 18 / 19 \\ 12 / 19 & 30 / 19\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}2 \\ 3\end{matrix}$$ The expected number of steps needed when starting at state $$2$$ before the chain is absorbed is the sum of the entries in the column of $$M$$ corresponding to state $$2$$ , which is $$\frac{30}{19} + \frac{12}{19} = \frac{42}{19}$$

Using the canonical form of the transition matrix, we see that $$& & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & & & & & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & S & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 / 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 / 3\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4\end{matrix} & \text{and} & A = S M & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}15 / 19 & 9 / 19 \\ 4 / 19 & 10 / 19\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4\end{matrix}$$ The probability that the chain is absorbed at state $$1$$ given that the Markov chain starts at state $$2$$ is the entry in $$A$$ whose row corresponds to state $$1$$ and whose column corresponds to state $$2$$ ; this entry is $$15/19$$ .

Reorder the states as $$\left\{ 4 \text{,} 1 \text{,} 2 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ and make state $$4$$ into an absorbing state to produce the canonical form $$& & \begin{matrix}4 & 1 & 2 & 3\end{matrix} & P & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 2 / 3 & 1 / 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{matrix}$$ So $$& & \begin{matrix}1 & 2 3\end{matrix} & & & & & \begin{matrix}1 & 2 & 3\end{matrix} & Q & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}2 / 3 & 1 / 2 & 0 \\ 1 / 3 & 1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{matrix} & \text{and} & M & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}14.25 & 11.25 & 6 . 75 \\ 7.50 & 7.50 & 4.50 \\ 3.00 & 3.00 & 3.00\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{matrix}$$ The expected number of steps required to reach state $$4$$ , starting at state $$2$$ , is the sum of the entries in the column of $$M$$ corresponding to state $$2$$ , which is $$\text{11} . \text{25} + \text{7} . \text{50} + \text{3} . \text{00} = \text{21} . \text{75}$$

Make states $$1$$ and $$4$$ into absorbing states and reorder the states as $$\left\{ 1 \text{,} 4, 2 \text{,} 3 \right\}$$ to produce the canonical form $$& & \begin{matrix}1 & 4 & 2 & 3\end{matrix} & P & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 & 0 & 1 / 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 / 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{matrix}$$ So $$& & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & & & & & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & & Q & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 / 6 & 1 / 2 \\ 1 / 3 & 1 / 6\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}2 \\ 3\end{matrix} & , & M & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}30 / 19 & 18 / 19 \\ 12 / 19 & 30 / 19\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}2 \\ 3\end{matrix} & ,$$ $$& & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & & & & & \begin{matrix}2 & 3\end{matrix} & S & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}1 / 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 / 3\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4\end{matrix} & \text{and} & A = S M & = & \begin{bmatrix} \begin{matrix}15 / 19 & 9 / 19 \\ 4 / 19 & 10 / 19\end{matrix} \end{bmatrix} & \begin{matrix}1 \\ 4\end{matrix}$$ Thus the probability that, starting at state $$2$$ , state $$1$$ is reached before state $$4$$ is the entry in $$A$$ whose row corresponds to state $$1$$ and whose column corresponds to state $$2$$ ; this entry is $$15/19$$ .
